hazard: Relevant observations not communicated to healthcare staff

concerns.quote: There is a lack of awareness amongst detention staff at Harmondsworth of: (i) behaviours (and reported experiences) which may indicate the existence of mental health issues affecting particular detainees- particularly in relation to schizophrenia; and (ii) the need to ensure that such potential indicators are brought to the attention of those responsible for the particular detainee's healthcare
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness of mental health indicators among detention staff

concerns.quote: Relevant and significant observations recorded by detention centre staff and others are not actively brought to the attention of relevant healthcare staff
concerns.hazard: relevant observations not communicated to healthcare staff

concerns.quote: Medical practitioners may be employed at Harmondsworth IRC without knowledge necessary to that role
Routine medical visits to segregated detainees are inadequate properly to assess detainees' healthcare needs
concerns.hazard: inadequate routine medical visits for segregated detainees

concerns.quote: The absence of a comprehensive and accessible (computerised) clinical record relating to each detainee at IRCs Harmondsworth and Colnbrook
concerns.hazard: absence of comprehensive accessible clinical records

concerns.quote: A GP who had seen Mr [name redacted]Tov during his stay at Colnbrook IRC told the jury that he never seen and was not aware of the content of ACDT documents and regarded the document as a custody officer process. He told the Court that it was not customary for healthcare staff to attend or participate in the ACDT process. This puts detainees at risk.
concerns.hazard: lack of healthcare staff participation in ACDT process

concerns.quote: The nurses who gave evidence similarly were uncertain of their role with respect to the ACDT process and had variable accounts of their involvement in the ACDT process. This puts detainees at risk.
concerns.hazard: uncertainty of nurses' role in ACDT process

concerns.quote: The Consultant [name redacted] psychiatrist did not read the ACDT documents. This puts detainees at risk.
concerns.hazard: failure of consultant forensic psychiatrist to read ACDT documents

concerns.quote: Mr [name redacted]Tov expressed that he might save his medication and take as an overdose. There was conflicting evidence as to the rigour of the checks to ensure detainees had swallowed issued medicine at the time of dispensing and the nurses who gave evidence described different practices of observation. Mr [name redacted]Tov was able to collect sufficient codeine ultimately to be able to end his life. This lack of consistency of checks puts detainee's at risk.

Mr [name redacted]Tov was taken to the Hillingdon Hospital in the late morning following his overdose on the 16th February 2016. At the Hillingdon Hospital an assessment, examination and blood tests were taken. The blood tests indicated renal impairment. An information system TOXBASE is used in emergency departments to provide assistance to clinicians. Toxbase indicates that in renal impairment greater care must be taken in cases of codeine overdose. This was missed.
concerns.hazard: failure to apply TOXBASE guidance for renal impairment in codeine overdose

concerns.quote: During the journey back to the Colnbrook IRC Mr [name redacted]Tov vomited several times. He vomited on his return to the healthcare unit. The nurse on duty was not told by the escorting custody staff and did not ask about any vomiting in the returning minibus. In oral evidence the nurse said that had he known of the vomiting then he would have returned Mr [name redacted]Tov to the hospital for further assessment. He did not know because he did not ask and was not told.
concerns.hazard: lack of communication about vomiting during transfer

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that important information observed or documented by detention/custody staff is not effectively communicated to healthcare personnel, putting detainees at risk. The earlier report concerns missed mental‑health observations; the later report concerns unawareness of ACDT documents and lack of healthcare staff participation in that process.
